messages.subject: ME/7104/25 Pennington/Halworth — Phase 1 outcome
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Whitfield,

I am writing to inform you that the CMA has found that the merger gives rise to a realistic prospect of a substantial lessening of competition in the supply of centrifugal and submersible pumps to the UK municipal water and wastewater sector. The full decision will follow shortly.

The CMA considers that your client's offer of undertakings in lieu (divestment of the Aqualis business) may be capable of remedying the concern, and we are minded to consider undertakings rather than refer at this stage. The case team will send comments on the draft undertakings this week.

Regards
Adrian Renton
Director of Mergers | Competition and Markets Authority

messages.snippet: Grace, Richard, As expected, the CMA has found a realistic prospect of an SLC confined to the munici
messages.subject: FW: Project Forge — Phase 1 outcome (good news on the path forward)
messages.plaintextBody:
Grace, Richard,

As expected, the CMA has found a realistic prospect of an SLC confined to the municipal-water frame — but crucially they are minded to accept undertakings in lieu rather than refer to Phase 2. That is the outcome we were working towards: it resolves matters at Phase 1 via the Aqualis divestment, and avoids a long and costly Phase 2.

Next step is negotiating the undertakings. We'll bring the draft to the board. I'd suggest a short board call to authorise the divestment in principle.

Best
Sarah

Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 0512
Confidential and may be legally privileged.
